name: Hollow Point // Concrete Saints Live Tee
description:
An unlicensed bootleg concert tee from the Concrete Saints' 2198 Hollow Point tour — the last tour they did before their lead vocalist, Priya Osei-Nakamura, lost her voice to a botched laryngeal augment surgery. The shirt is printed on a thin, slightly translucent synth-cotton blend that's already turning grey at the collar seams. The front graphic is a stylized saint's halo rendered as a cracked highway interchange, with the band's name in a compressed sans-serif below. The back lists twelve cities, four of which are neighborhoods in GLMZ rather than actual cities.

These were sold out of a duffel bag at the venue exits and from a handful of Shelf-adjacent street stalls for a few weeks after the tour ended. The print quality varies — some have ghosting on the halo, some have the city list slightly off-center. Nobody cares. The Saints have a cult following among Shelf punks, Tier 2 youth, and a certain kind of Tier 3 person who wants to signal they were there before the band got complicated.
what_it_says: You were there, or you want people to think you were. Either way, you know who the Concrete Saints are, and that's enough to get a nod from the right people in the right neighborhoods.
worn_by: anyone who mourns what the Saints used to be
story_hooks: Priya Osei-Nakamura is supposedly working with a rogue biotech outfit on an experimental vocal cord replacement — someone wearing this shirt in the wrong place might get approached by a recruiter looking for people who still believe in her.
One specific print run of this shirt has a micro-QR code accidentally embedded in the halo graphic — scanning it opens an encrypted dead drop that nobody has claimed in two years.
A Tier 4 corporate fixer has been quietly buying up every authentic Hollow Point tee they can find; nobody knows why, but the price on the secondary market has started to climb.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn concert tee with faded graphic presence, slightly slouchy and deliberately under-constructed. The print has visible ghosting and imperfections that read as authenticity rather than defect. On-body, it communicates nostalgia mixed with underground credibility—the wearer is claiming presence at a pivotal moment in GLMZ music history.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, slightly oversized through the body and shoulders. Not tailored—cuts are generous and comfortable, designed for layering under jackets or mesh overlays. Armholes are roomy, hem hits mid-hip.
physical_description.primary_material: Synth-cotton blend, thin and slightly translucent in direct light. Budget construction with minimal weight—the fabric moves easily against the body.
physical_description.texture: Soft from wear but paper-thin. Seams are visible and slightly raised. The print itself has a matte, slightly cracked surface where inks are breaking down. Collar seams show grey oxidation staining.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded black base with washed-out grey undertones. Front graphic in degraded white and pale grey, with hints of the original brighter ink showing through cracks. Back text similarly faded. Overall impression of aged silver-grey.
physical_description.closures: None—simple pullover crew neck with ribbed collar and cuffs.
distinctive_features: Cracked highway interchange halo graphic with visible print ghosting
Compressed sans-serif band name slightly pixelated from bootleg printing
Back printed city list with four GLMZ neighborhood names (Shelf, Milltown, Dockside, etc.) instead of actual cities
Visible manufacturing inconsistencies—off-center alignment on some examples
Oxidized grey staining at collar seams from age and wear
Intentionally imperfect print quality that signals unlicensed origin
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 cultural artifact. The bootleg nature and worn condition signal street-level authenticity, not corporate polish. Worn by those claiming grassroots credibility rather than wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Shelf punk, underground music culture, nostalgia for pre-tragedy band era. Wearer signals they were there, they know the deep cuts, they exist outside official distribution. Minor flex of counterculture knowledge mixed with genuine fandom.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily worn, faded, slightly dingy. Print degradation is expected and valued. Seams intact but collar showing stress. The worse it looks, the more genuine the claim of long-term ownership.
